comment: Eight shared developer lanes on the 16-Spark fleet (PR #1082 baseline). One driver family per lane. Budgets are per node per lane; the eight lanes together must stay inside the verified envelope: 78336 MiB total reservation + 8192 MiB queue headroom per Spark. Ports: lane L owns control 23000+16L .. +15, collective 53000+16L .. +15 (u16-valid, clear of every fleet_registry block), transport 64000+16L .. +15. Exclusive reservations are MANAGER-AUTHORIZED ONLY (phase 2, critical benchmarks); routine work is smoke tests + small B* under shared lanes with same-conditions A/B discipline.

conventions: Ceph law (operator directive 2026-09-22): every ceph read comes through one of the 16 per-node clients (one shared mount; client health varies per node). NVMe is the only serving source. Per family/topology: FIRST search the fleet NVMe inventory (the placed pack sets use their historical names — e.g. qwenmax.*, not new conventions; the operator's expectation is the map). If found: use it, zero ceph. If not found: the owning dev generates the stagepack via ONE-TIME ceph reads through the healthiest client, single large-scale reader fleet-wide, output lands on NVMe with receipts — and ceph is never read again for that artifact.

Review boundary (operator directive 2026-09-23): every change OUTSIDE the model driver itself (shared tools, runtime/, ring/, include/, cache/, queue tooling, templates, fleet unit files, registry, docs, this table) lands as a PR — never direct to fleet or main — with shared-infrastructure changes in clearly separable, dedicated PRs (not riders inside family-milestone PRs) so a returning reviewer can audit them standalone.

Queue truth is the CONTROLLER ledger only: every spark_queue.py call runs via ssh mac@mac-studio in /Users/mac/wk-sparkpipe-queue-main-20260922. A local worktree ledger is a dead state file that reports fiction (lane 3 incident).
Ledger regen law (three paid variants): regen LAST after all edits; git status --porcelain empty of untracked immediately before; verify_package_manifest against COMMITTED content before push.

Local-gate recipe (Actions-stall fallback): sync exact head to sparkb via the controller, CPU job ttl 15 mem 16384, sequence = generate_k3_contract --check, generate_dsv4_contracts --check, tests/test_must_work_targets.py, then NVCC=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc CUDA_ARCH=sm_121a SPARK_CUDA_GATE_SCOPE=complete tools/cuda13_sm121a_compile_gate.sh with PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin prefix (cuobjdump). Manager merges on green receipt + head verify.

Arena policy: pack/expert bytes ride the shared weightd arena (tracked 29,184 MiB/node, additional to lane budgets). Default posture: one attached pack per node; subset-attach families coexist while the declared per-node arena sum stays <= ~24 GiB. Never rely on eviction between GPU jobs.
Lane budget = resident side only (KV, workspace, activations, resident spine). Manifests present BOTH views: resident-inclusive and lane-job-only.

Preload model (operator directive 2026-09-22): expert tracing is one-time; the manifest IS the permanent working-set definition. New instances batch-preload the entire traced set at launch; the shared weightd daemon holds it resident for its lifetime so every subsequent instance launch reads from RAM. Only a weightd restart re-triggers the slow load. M3 receipts therefore report THREE numbers: (1) daemon cold-warm elapsed (once per daemon lifetime), (2) instance time_to_ready against a warm daemon (the <5 s target), (3) steady-state serve rate from RAM. The <5 s claim is number (2), never number (1).
Smoke sets are small by design: canonical prompt set preloads <= ~2 GiB/node; lazy attach covers strays; manifests record only what the canonical set touches.

Build jobs may exceed lane serving budgets with honest declared reservations + bounded TTL (nvcc -j4 RSS is real); serving jobs stay inside the lane table. Keep queue cmd files dollar-free (systemd expands $-syntax).
